question.text: Under SEBI's framework for performance benchmarking of AIFs (Circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF6/CIR/P/2020/24 read with the June 12, 2020 circular), any association of AIFs that notifies one or more Benchmarking Agencies must represent at least what percentage of the number of AIFs?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** As per the SEBI circulars on disclosure standards for AIFs, 'any association of AIFs which in terms of membership, represents at least 33 percent of the number of AIFs, may notify one or more Benchmarking Agencies.' IVCA (Indian Private Equity and Venture Capital Association) meets this threshold and has notified CRISIL, NSE and Preqin as benchmarking agencies. **The Trap:** Options A (10%), B (25%), and D (50%) are plausible regulatory thresholds — 10% and 25% echo the Cat III concentration limits (single-investee 10% open-ended / 25% close-ended), and 50% echoes quorum rules — but the specific benchmarking-association threshold is 33%. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C and XIX-D both test this 33% threshold for benchmarking-agency notification. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests it from the sell-side disclosure angle. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** The Cat III manager must contractually enter into an agreement with the notified benchmarking agency within one year of First Close — confidentiality clauses in this agreement are standard, and the agency reports back a 'Benchmark Report' vs the industry benchmark, which you must disclose in all marketing material and investor reports going forward.
